answers.question: Where in the code are bill line items priced from a stock item or billable service, and how does that pricing get applied?

paragraphs.text: Pricing of bill line items happens in two places depending on where the bill comes from: at the POS (point-of-sale) form in the frontend, where a cashier's chosen price is copied into the line item; and in the backend billing strategies, where a price is resolved automatically for a stock item or a billable service.
## What the pieces are

A bill line item is a `BillLineItem` [1]. It can point at a **stock item** (a physical commodity from the stock management module) or at a **billable service** (a service, e.g. a lab test, tied to a concept), and it carries a `price` plus a `priceName`:

- `item` — the `StockItem` [2]
- `billableService` — the `BillableService` [3]
- `price` and `priceName` — the amount and its label [4]
- `getTotal()` multiplies the unit price by quantity [5], and the bill total sums each line's total [6]

The list of prices itself is the `CashierItemPrice` entity [7] — a named price with a `paymentMode`, attached to either a `StockItem` or a `BillableService`. A `BillableService` exposes its prices as `servicePrices` [8].
## Path 1: pricing at the POS form
The frontend loads billable services together with their prices — the query asks for `servicePrices:(uuid,name,price,paymentMode)` [9].
When the cashier picks an item, `selectBillableItem` reads that item's available payment methods (`servicePrices`) [10]\) and builds a line item:

- If there is exactly **one** price, it is taken automatically as the default [11].
- The line item is created with `price: defaultPrice`, `billableService: item.uuid` and status `PENDING` [12].
- If there are several prices, the cashier must choose one via `updatePaymentMethod`, which sets `price`, `priceName` and `priceUuid` from the chosen `ServicePrice` [13]. `validateSelectedItems` blocks submission until a payment method is chosen for any item with more than one price [14].

On submit, `postBillItems` maps the selected items to `LineItem` payloads carrying `price`, `quantity`, `billableService` and status `PENDING` [15], then POSTs to the bill endpoint [16]. In edit mode it also re-sends each existing line item with its stored `price`, `priceName` and `priceUuid` [17]. The `LineItem` type shows `price`, `priceName` and `priceUuid` as the fields that carry pricing [18].

On the server, the REST layer writes those values onto the entity: `setPriceValue` converts the incoming number to a `BigDecimal` [19], `setPriceName` stores the label [20], and `setItemPrice` (the `priceUuid` property) is meant to attach the chosen `CashierItemPrice` [21]. Note that this `setItemPrice` is effectively a stub right now: `itemPrice` is assigned `null` and never looked up, so the UUID sent by the UI is not resolved to a real price record [22]; the getter likewise ignores the stored price and returns an empty string [23]. In practice the amount the cashier picked travels in the `price` field itself.
## Path 2: automatic pricing from an order

When a clinician places an order, a **billing strategy** per order type builds the bill automatically. The shared pipeline resolves cashier and cash point, creates the `Bill`, attaches the line item and saves [24]. The common line-item fields are set by `createLineItem`, which assigns the `price`, quantity, status and order [25].

**Drug order → stock item.** `DrugOrderBillingStrategy` handles `DrugOrder`s [26]. It looks up the `StockItem` for the ordered drug via `stockManagementService.getStockItemByDrug(drugId)` [27], then calls `resolvePrice(stockItem)` and sets the stock item on the line item [28]. `resolvePrice` asks `itemPriceService.getItemPrice(stockItem)` and, if any `CashierItemPrice` exists, uses the first one's price; otherwise it falls back to the stock item's `purchasePrice`, and finally to zero [29].

**Test order → billable service.** `TestOrderBillingStrategy` handles `TestOrder`s [30]. It finds the enabled `BillableService` whose concept matches the test order's concept [31], then calls `resolvePrice(billableService)` and attaches the service [32]. Its `resolvePrice` uses `itemPriceService.getServicePrice(billableService)` and takes the first price, defaulting to zero if none exists [33]. Quantity is fixed at 1, since a test is treated as a single service [34].
## Where the price records are looked up
Both `resolvePrice` methods go through `ItemPriceService`:

- `getItemPrice(StockItem)` queries `CashierItemPrice` by `item` and orders by id descending, so the newest price wins [35].
- `getServicePrice(BillableService)` queries by `billableService`, also newest first [36].
## The flow at a glance

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    order["Order placed"] --> pick{"Order type"}
    pick -->|DrugOrder| drug["Find StockItem by drug"]
    pick -->|TestOrder| svc["Find enabled BillableService by concept"]
    drug --> ip["getItemPrice newest CashierItemPrice"]
    ip --> fallback["Fallback to StockItem purchasePrice"]
    svc --> sp["getServicePrice newest CashierItemPrice"]
    fallback --> item["createLineItem price"]
    sp --> item
    item --> bill["Bill.addLineItem and save"]
    pos["POS form picks item"] --> formPrice["price from servicePrices"]
    formPrice --> post["POST bill line item price"]
```
## Summary

The single stored value is `BillLineItem.price` [37], multiplied by quantity in `getTotal()` [5]. `priceName` records which named price was used. The source of that price is either the cashier's choice on the POS form (frontend) or, for orders, the newest matching `CashierItemPrice` for the stock item or billable service, with a fallback to the stock item's purchase price for drugs and to zero for services.

What I could not verify: I did not read the full `BillLineItemResource` (only lines 100-169) or the cash-point/bill discount code paths, and I did not trace how `CashierItemPrice` records are created in the admin UI — only how they are read. The `setItemPrice` handler [21] looks like unfinished code, so the `priceUuid` sent by the frontend may not persist as a link to a `CashierItemPrice`; the numeric `price` is what actually takes effect.
